Scope and method
Read only the implementation report, the six named changed source/docs/test/build files, and the checked-in prefill source around the routing-readback call and layer-major request retirement. No build, test, lint, AST, GPU/model, profiler, runtime log/environment/process query, cleanup, commit, or mutation outside this report. This is a source audit, not performance, correctness-on-device, or numerical qualification.

Finding
No source-level correctness defect found in the bounded union calculation or its production observation placement. The route is observed once per MoE layer per layer-major chunk at a shared point before CPU expert grouping, MMQ, compact-MoE, native expert, and ordinary expert execution split into their distinct handling paths. The point follows ids_host.from_device(m.ids, m.cs) and the existing checked stream_sync(m.cs); the host vector was resized to T*K. The observer receives the current layer, c0 row offset, T rows, host route IDs and layer blob extent. Source lines: src/prefill/prefill.cpp:2288–2311; downstream branch points begin after 2330.

Geometry and coverage
run_layer_major iterates each layer over the complete request, and run_impl chunks it with c0=0,m.T,... and T=min(m.T,n-c0) (src/prefill/prefill.cpp:1537–1590, 1664–1668). Thus the final short chunk is included with its exact T, including a host/GPU residual boundary when configured; route collection is upstream of those residual-store choices. PLE's attention/history handling occurs independently before the MoE route point. The census validates offset continuity, positive rows/blob, exact T*K IDs, ID range 0..511, constant per-layer blob extent, layer order, expected chunk cap, and final per-layer row/chunk coverage. Its per-chunk 512-bit local set increments active_visits by distinct experts in that chunk and unique by newly observed experts across the request. The fixture's overlap case distinguishes 20 visits from 18 union experts. Header lines 10–106.

Lifetime and failure status
The receipt is allocated only after request admission and only for the exact opt-in. Its owner is declared before Restore, so reverse destruction runs Restore while the receipt remains alive. Restore's layer_major::retire first cancels staging, drains compute and copy streams, finishes the stager, then clears the borrowed Impl pointer and emits. A failed drain enters the existing fail callback and cannot emit success. union_success becomes true only after every per-layer run_impl returns successfully; every earlier return/exception/cancellation leaves it false. finish independently requires expected full coverage and checked per-layer and aggregate logical-byte arithmetic. The receipt retains no token routes beyond the request. Source lines: 1483–1521, 1537–1590; helper include/strata/prefill/route_union.hpp:66–105.

Opt-in/default behavior
The switch uses exact string equality with "1" and is frozen per layer-major request local check; the shared inference route and IDs are unchanged. With it OFF, no RouteUnion allocation, observation, output, added kernel/copy/event/sync/wait/clock occurs; only the null pointer guard at the common route point and opt-in checks remain. With it ON on an unsupported flow/empty request, one decline summary is emitted, while normal inference eligibility is not altered. The source/docs explicitly scope byte figures as logical extents, not measured PCIe traffic or actual upload reduction. This remains true: current layer-major upload still loads all 512 experts per layer.

Small reporting caveat
For partial/invalid measurements, per-layer extent_valid reports only whether multiplication by the recorded blob value overflowed. A layer with blob_bytes=0 can therefore show extent_valid=1 and zero logical extents while status=partial/invalid. The status prevents a false complete result; still, the field name can be read as certifying a meaningful blob extent. Consider either requiring c.blob != 0 in this field or renaming it to extent_arithmetic_valid before any consumer relies on partial rows. This does not affect successful records.

Main-owned next validation
1. Run the new CPU fixture under the repository warning flags, then verify CMake target/CTest registration in Main's owned build.
2. On the established qualified hardware/model path, run two separate fresh GEN requests with exact opt-in and compare per-layer rows/chunks to accepted prompt geometry; confirm second-request reset and no duplicate observation. Exercise one cancellation/early failure and require partial/invalid, never complete.
3. Confirm a stock run with the switch unset has unchanged output/math and no census records; keep GPU/trace ownership and retention serialized. Do not infer speedup, PCIe savings, or numerical qualification from this census alone.
